title: Difficulty Calibration Audit — Distribution Analysis

case_study_difficulty.note: Case studies have 35.7% Difficult (vs 3.3% MCQ) — much better calibrated. Zero VDiff same as MCQ.

root_cause.primary: Template-rotation authoring pipeline assigned difficulty and Bloom's labels by rotation position, not cognitive assessment
root_cause.secondary: No Analyze/Evaluate items were ever authored. 96.7% Understand+Apply creates a bimodal pool incapable of reaching the upper difficulty tiers.
root_cause.structural: DL-031 (definition-match items labeled Moderate) inflates the Moderate band by ~800-1,000 items, masking the true difficulty profile.

phase_1_recalibration_plan.approach: Coordinated sweep: ~807 items recalibrated across all 5 packs to reach Phase 1 intermediate targets
phase_1_recalibration_plan.execution_order: C → D → B → A → E (simplest to most complex)
phase_1_recalibration_plan.note: Very Difficult bridge limited to 22 feasible recalibrations (0.87%) — Phase 2 content creation needed for full 10%

critical_findings: F-01: ZERO Very Difficult items (0/2,540) — no learner practice at the hardest exam tier
F-02: Only 85 Difficult items (3.3%) — CMA exam has ~25% Difficult items
F-03: Moderate inflated by 18.3pp (48.3% vs 30% target) — 464 items surplus
F-04: ZERO Evaluate items (0/2,540) — no professional judgment testing
F-05: Analyze+Evaluate combined = 0.4% vs 40% target — 39.6pp gap
F-06: Understand+Apply = 96.7% — the pool cannot simulate actual CMA cognitive demands
F-07: DL-031 affects 800-1,000 items — definition-match items labeled Moderate
F-08: Pack A has zero Difficult items despite 96.2% certification — worst calibration
F-09: Pack E is 77% Understand — functions as a terminology quiz, not an exam section
F-10: Bloom's and Difficulty gaps are causally linked — requiring content expansion, not just relabeling
